what: Snowflake sells a cloud data platform. Companies load their data into it, query it, share it with partners and now build AI applications on top. Customers pay for the compute and storage they actually use.
customers: Large and mid-sized companies in every industry, running their analytics and data warehouses on it.
money: consumption-based charges for compute and storage
moat: Data gravity: once a company's data and its queries live in Snowflake, moving them is expensive, and its data-sharing network adds value with each participant.
risks: It is not profitable on reported earnings and lost about $1.1 billion over the last twelve months
Stock-based compensation is very large relative to revenue
The big cloud providers sell competing services and also host it
Consumption pricing means revenue falls immediately if customers optimise their usage
opportunities: Revenue is still growing around 29% a year with gross margins near 67%
AI workloads increase the amount of data companies want to store and query
Net revenue retention above 100% means existing customers keep spending more
watch: Product revenue growth, net revenue retention and whether free cash flow keeps improving.
